about: Recurring cast of the retro modern illustration Shorts (format "retro"). Drawn by shorts/design_kit/retro-kit.jsx (RMArthur / RMMae / RMHuman, RMCritic, RMHand) — never redraw a cast member by hand. Append each episode to the character's history.
style: Mid-century editorial illustration: vermilion / indigo / pink / mustard / cream / black only, stippled grain, angular faces with big triangle noses and yellow eyes, hatched hair and moustaches, glowing cyan electricity as the one accent. Reference: shorts/styles/retro/.

arthur.name: Arthur
arthur.look: pink square face, red triangle nose, hatched black hair, moustache, black suit
arthur.personality: earnest office worker who takes everything to heart; replays every comment
history: ep 1 (arthur-the-critic): negativity bias — 10 compliments, 1 criticism, replays it at 2 AM; the Critic is 'a very old alarm'; tonight Arthur talks back
ep 2 (peak-end-rule, with Mae): six perfect holiday days + one cancelled flight = 'a total disaster'; Mae shows him the chart (peak-end rule, Kahneman et al. 1993) and ends every meeting on a high
ep 3 (thirty-six-questions, with Otto + Mae): answers the 36 questions with Otto; shares a name with psychologist Arthur Aron
ep 4 (tapping-song): cameo — sweating before Otto's software training
ep 5 (otto-quiz-night, with Otto): sure he bombed quiz night, finishes near the top; his "maybe I don't know" is the skill (Dunning-Kruger effect, Kruger & Dunning 1999)

ep 6 (arthur-3am-worries, with The Doubt): wide awake at 3 AM while The Doubt whispers "what if" (the email, the meeting, the car noise); writes each worry down and checks later; worry's deceit (LaFreniere & Newman 2020: ~91% of worry predictions in people with GAD never came true)
ep 7 (otto-rhyme-poster): nods at Otto's rhyming poster, then fixes it: "Work late. Feel tired."

ep 8 (arthur-ask-favour, with Otto): needs a favour from grumpy Otto and would rather struggle alone; Ben Franklin effect (Jecker & Landy 1969: people the researcher personally asked to return their winnings liked him more); borrows Otto's pen, next day Otto says hello
ep 9 (mae-rainy-holiday, with Mae): flicks through Mae's sunny album and points out it rained; rosy retrospection (Mitchell et al. 1997)

critic.name: The Critic
critic.look: indigo creature, red-spotted dome head, droopy yellow eyes, fangs, long blue fingers
critic.personality: Arthur's inner critic: sarcastic, dramatic, presses 'the button' — but really an ancient alarm trying to protect him. Can personify any bias (the voice that lies).
history: ep 1 (arthur-the-critic): introduced
ep 2 (mae-liking-gap): visits Mae's head, replays her small talk; shrinks when the neighbour knocks with cookies
ep 3 (lila-replay-write): hits replay on Lila's "thanks, Mum"; pressed flat onto a notebook page he's just a boring paragraph

mae.name: Mae
mae.look: mustard face, indigo bob with a red clip, red lips, green jacket
mae.personality: sharp, warm colleague; asks the one question that breaks the spell
history: ep 1 (peak-end-rule, with Arthur): asks how the trip was, shows him 6 of 7 days were great; her tip: end dates, workouts and meetings on a high
ep 2 (scarcity-cookies, with Lila): shows Lila a full tray of the 'only two left' cookies in the back
ep 3 (thirty-six-questions): hands Otto and Arthur the list of 36 questions

ep 4 (mae-liking-gap, with the Critic): five minutes of small talk with her new neighbour; the Critic replays it all night ('that joke? awful'); liking gap (Boothby et al. 2018); next morning the neighbour brings cookies
ep 5 (lila-group-photo, with Lila): shrugs off Lila's selfie panic: "nobody inspects your face like you do" (cheerleader effect, Walker & Vul 2014)
ep 6 (lila-replay-write): hands Lila a pen: "fifteen minutes, then close the notebook"

ep 7 (mae-too-many-shows, with The Doubt): endless choices on her streaming app, scrolls forty minutes and watches nothing; choice overload (Iyengar & Lepper 2000 jam study: 24 jams ~3% of stoppers bought, 6 jams ~30%); picks from three and is watching in a minute

ep 8 (mae-rainy-holiday, with Arthur): holiday photos look perfect though it rained for three days; laughs that her memory kept the good parts; rosy retrospection (Mitchell, Thompson, Peterson & Cronk 1997: bike tour 5% expected disappointment, 61% disappointed during, 11% remembered it a week later)

otto.name: Otto
otto.look: bald cream head with forehead lines, monobrow-heavy brows, blue suit, red tie
otto.personality: Arthur's boss: loud, certain, rarely right; authority and status effects
history: ep 1 (stroop-test): says no test can trick him; Lila's colour-word card does (Stroop effect) — his brain is too good at reading

ep 2 (thirty-six-questions, with Arthur + Mae): ten years at the next desk, knows one fact (Arthur likes tea); the 36 questions (Aron et al. 1997) leave him wiping his eyes; brings Arthur a tea next morning

ep 3 (tapping-song, with Lila + Arthur): taps Happy Birthday on his desk, sure it's 'EASY'; Lila guesses Morse code (curse of knowledge, Newton 1990: 3 of 120 songs); tomorrow he trains the whole office — Arthur already sweating, PART 2

ep 4 (otto-quiz-night, with Arthur): sure he crushed quiz night ("EASY!"), comes LAST; Dunning-Kruger effect (Kruger & Dunning 1999: bottom-quarter scorers averaged around the 12th percentile but guessed around the 62nd)
ep 5 (lila-replay-write): cameo in Lila's replay as the boss she called "Mum"

ep 6 (otto-rhyme-poster, with Arthur): hangs a rhyming poster "Work late, feel great"; rhyme-as-reason effect (McGlone & Tofighbakhsh 2000: "woes unite foes" rated more accurate than "woes unite enemies")

ep 7 (otto-name-it, with Lila): furious when the printer jams before his big meeting, types in caps, insists he's fine; affect labeling (Lieberman et al. 2007: naming the feeling lowered amygdala activity); Lila asks 'Frustrated?' and his jaw unclenches
ep 8 (arthur-ask-favour, with Arthur): lends Arthur his pen and is suddenly friendly the next day

ep 9 (otto-hungry-shop, with Lila): went in for milk, came out with six snacks; hot-cold empathy gap (Read & van Leeuwen 1998: 200 Amsterdam workers chose a snack for next week; hungry choosers picked more junk); Lila hands him a banana first
ep 10 (lila-lucky-numbers, with Lila): hands out random office-lottery tickets; shrugs at Lila's 'lucky' birthday numbers

lila.name: Lila
lila.look: pink face, big mustard curls, red jacket
lila.personality: bold new intern; says what she thinks, gets swept up by the crowd
history: ep 1 (stroop-test, with Otto): holds up the Stroop cards for her boss

ep 2 (scarcity-cookies, with The Doubt + Mae): not hungry, sees 'only 2 left', The Doubt whispers 'what if they're gone?', buys both (scarcity effect, Worchel, Lee & Adewole 1975); new rule: would I want it if there were ten?
ep 3 (tapping-song, with Otto): hears only knocking when Otto taps Happy Birthday; guesses Morse code

ep 4 (lila-group-photo, with Mae): hates her solo selfie but loves the group photo, same face; cheerleader effect (Walker & Vul 2014: same face rated more attractive in a group than cropped alone — tiny, ~49th to 51st percentile)

ep 5 (lila-replay-write, with The Critic, Mae): replays the meeting where she called her boss "Mum"; expressive writing (Pennebaker & Beall 1986: 15 min × 4 days, fewer health-centre visits over six months); closes the notebook
ep 6 (otto-name-it, with Otto): asks her boss 'Frustrated?' — naming it calms him (affect labeling)

ep 7 (lila-train-stranger, with The Doubt): morning train, headphones in, eyes down while The Doubt hisses 'it'll be awkward'; mistakenly seeking solitude (Epley & Schroeder 2014: Chicago commuters who talked to a stranger had a more pleasant ride, though they predicted the opposite); asks 'Good book?' and twenty minutes vanish
ep 8 (otto-hungry-shop, with Otto): hands Otto a banana before he shops; 'eat, then shop'

ep 9 (lila-lucky-numbers, with Otto): office lottery, won't take Otto's random ticket and picks her birthday; illusion of control (Langer 1975: $1 tickets, chose-own asked $8.67 to sell vs $1.96 handed); puts the rest into savings

doubt.name: The Doubt
doubt.look: mustard pear-shaped creature, one big eye, pink spots, skinny ink limbs
doubt.personality: the 'what if…' voice: whispers worst cases, second-guesses decisions (anxiety, impostor feelings, analysis paralysis); a rival to The Critic
history: ep 1 (scarcity-cookies, with Lila): introduced — whispers 'what if they're gone?' at an 'only 2 left' sign; shrinks when Lila asks 'would I want it if there were ten?'
ep 2 (arthur-3am-worries, with Arthur): whispers "what if…" at 3 AM; gets stamped WRONG and shrinks once Arthur writes his worries down and checks them (LaFreniere & Newman 2020)
ep 3 (mae-too-many-shows, with Mae): whispers 'what if the other one's better?' over a long menu (choice overload)
ep 4 (lila-train-stranger, with Lila): hisses 'it'll be awkward' on the train; shrinks to a pea when Lila says hi
